leftEvidence.title: Abner turns toward covenant with David

points.label: Action and response
points.left: War continues as David’s house grows stronger; after conflict with Ishbosheth, Abner negotiates, Michal is returned, and elders hear his proposal.
points.right: Joab recalls Abner, kills him at Hebron, and David publicly distances himself through curse, mourning, fasting, and lament while confessing weakness before powerful commanders.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a transfer of allegiance approaches through disputed household and political claims inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places public lament separates David from a murder he says he cannot control inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 3:1–21 and 2 Samuel 3:22–39 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Judah, Conflict, and Unification” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Joab kills Abner and David laments

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 3:1–21 foregrounds a transfer of allegiance approaches through disputed household and political claims; 2 Samuel 3:22–39 foregrounds public lament separates David from a murder he says he cannot control. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
